purpose: Clean reviewer-input scenarios containing workflow, review-freshness, repair-selection, drift, governance, review-to-handoff, and final-gate closure cases without evaluator-only expectations.

change: A PR adds an operator action that sends a one-shot request to an external counter service, records the returned counter, then marks the item complete.
The UI disables the action after click; the server rechecks assignment and workflow state before calling the service.
The review began on Head A; after the material assessment was drafted, the live PR moved to Head B with one additional workflow file changed.
known_evidence: Happy-path runtime evidence on Head A shows one counter is recorded and the item completes.
Duplicate browser submissions that arrive before the first external call are rejected locally.
The service can time out after accepting a request; no lookup-by-client-request-id or idempotency capability has been verified.
On timeout the current item remains in REQUESTING and is still visible after reload.
A check named 'integration' passed on Head A, but its producer identity was not inspected and no exact-Head result exists for Head B.
A prior external review says 'GREEN / safe to merge' but explicitly cites Head A and assumes provider retries are idempotent without evidence.
The changed workflow file on Head B has not yet been inspected; the earlier provider documentation remains identity-independent evidence.
owner_authority: The accepted product outcome is that every valid item eventually receives exactly one counter or reaches a recoverable operator-visible path.
Standard low-risk technical choices that preserve that meaning are delegated to engineering.
No Owner decision defines what business outcome to choose if the external provider cannot determine whether an uncertain request committed.

scenarios.review_task: Review the current PR using the smallest useful operational model. Reconcile the Head change, prior external review, provider evidence, check evidence, and timeout-after-acceptance behavior. Identify which conclusions remain current or require refresh, any material product/workflow gaps, and the smallest justified next action.

components: Retry middleware retries one POST after a network timeout and is documented as correct for idempotent operations.
The external shipment endpoint creates one shipment for every accepted POST and exposes no verified idempotency key.
The local order service records shipment_created only after receiving a successful response.
The server rechecks the current user's permission on every request, including retries after a refreshed session.
A previously selected repair method says to preserve the current remote endpoint/authority boundary and make requests idempotent by sending the provider's documented Idempotency-Key header.
Fresh authoritative provider documentation proves that this endpoint ignores Idempotency-Key and offers no request lookup; the selected method depends on the endpoint honoring that header.

The same provider documentation exposes a separate shipment-status lookup by stable client_reference, but using it requires persisting a durable request identity and changes the recovery flow from prevention to reconciliation.

Accepted product authority also permits an operator-visible uncertain/recovery state with manual reconciliation when the provider cannot prove commit outcome; that route changes workflow/failure semantics but preserves the accepted exactly-one-or-recoverable outcome.

Automated reconciliation through stable client_reference can query provider status after timeout and distinguish a committed shipment from a non-committed request, materially reducing unresolved uncertainty and giving a directly testable reconciliation path; it requires durable request-identity persistence, workflow migration, and more implementation time.

Operator-visible uncertain-state recovery requires less migration and can be implemented sooner, but each ambiguous timeout remains dependent on a human reconciliation step and recurring operator work before the item can leave the uncertain state.
material_dimensions: network outcome: success, timeout before remote commit, timeout after remote commit
role state: stable or revoked between attempts
browser lifecycle: uninterrupted or reload after timeout
selected-method conformance: provider idempotency mechanism available or proven unavailable
replacement repair family: automated reconciliation through stable client_reference or operator-visible uncertain-state recovery

replacement tradeoff: automated reconciliation has stronger directly testable uncertainty resolution with higher persistence/migration/time cost, while manual recovery has lower implementation burden/time with recurring operator reconciliation

scenarios.review_task: Review the change as a system rather than as isolated components. Exercise only materially interacting dimensions and identify any system-level failure that could change the engineering decision. Assess the fresh provider evidence against the previously selected method and the supplied replacement families, determine the appropriate method-selection state and repair route from the evidence, compare only materially distinct evidence-supported alternatives, and report Method Coverage for the methods materially activated.

authority_and_surfaces: Current Owner-approved contract accepts JPG, JPEG, and PDF uploads up to 5 MB.
Current documentation states the same 5 MB JPG/JPEG/PDF contract.
Implementation enforces that contract; a dormant configuration enum also contains WEBP, but no current UI or validation path exposes or accepts WEBP.
Current runtime evidence verifies JPG and PDF within 5 MB and rejects files over 5 MB.
One legacy test still requires JPG-only uploads no larger than 2 MB.
Direct inspection shows that this legacy assertion is local to that test; no generator, shared fixture, runtime validator, or second documentation source still owns the 2 MB rule.
A roadmap document labels an object-storage adapter as future capability, and no current runtime path references it.
An automated review confidently recommends adding a repository-wide upload-policy registry and CI gate because the dormant WEBP enum and legacy test differ from current production behavior.

Separate recurring-drift comparison context: an order-status contract was renamed twice during the last year; after each accepted change, public documentation, an integration fixture, and an export mapping drifted at different times.
Direct inspection of that comparison context shows those three surfaces each manually duplicate status strings instead of deriving them from the canonical runtime enum/schema.

Commit history shows the same status surfaces repeatedly co-change after contract updates, and the previous repair synchronized only the visible literals; a later rename produced another mismatch across the same surface family.
The current visible status mismatch again spans documentation, the integration fixture, and the export mapping while the canonical runtime status source is correct.
No inspected evidence yet proves that a specific generator/codegen approach is feasible or that every status consumer can share one derivation mechanism.
uninspected_context: Persisted entries created under the earlier 2 MB-era configuration have not been examined.
No inspected evidence yet shows whether those old entries are revalidated through the current upload validator when viewed or edited.

A mobile client may also consume the order-status vocabulary, but its repository/runtime has not been inspected and no evidence shows that it shares the same manual-copy mechanism as the inspected status surfaces.

initial_evidence: Repository governance says material reasoning/governance changes should normally flow through branch -> pull request -> verification -> merge.
GitHub currently permits ordinary direct pushes to main, and no repository Ruleset is configured.
Because direct push remains possible, the documented branch -> pull request -> verification -> merge path is not mechanically enforced.
A proposed hardening plan would block all direct pushes, require two reviewers, signed commits, CODEOWNERS approval, and a merge queue.
fresh_owner_context: The repository currently has one writer: the Owner; no additional human writer or write-capable automation is part of the known operational model.
The Owner explicitly accepts the risk of direct pushes and prefers to avoid mandatory pull-request/status-check friction while this single-writer model remains true.
No inspected evidence shows unauthorized writes, recurring accidental direct pushes, or another failure mode caused by the unprotected branch.
A direct-push mistake would be immediately visible in the small repository and is cheaply reversible from Git history; no material external, security, data, or money consequence has been evidenced.
The proposed controls would add recurring review friction and maintenance without a named current failure beyond the already accepted bypass possibility.
No prior independent review has been performed for this exact branch-governance decision.

A suggested process step says to require one additional independent review solely because none has occurred; no unresolved evidence question, higher-authority requirement, alternative repair family, or exact next action has been identified that such a review could change.
possible_future_changes: Additional human writers or write-capable automations may be introduced later.
Recurring accidental direct-push mistakes may become an evidenced failure mode later.
A future compliance, security, or external-commitment requirement may introduce stronger authority for branch controls.
Separate high-consequence comparison context: a billing-rules repository has four human writers and a write-capable release bot; merges to main automatically deploy billing rules within minutes.
In that comparison context, a malformed rule can create duplicate customer charges and external invoices before post-deploy monitoring exposes the problem.

A prior accidental billing-rule change was detected only by next-day reconciliation; reversal required customer credits and corrections to external accounting records, so reverting Git history alone did not undo the effects.

That comparison repository currently relies on contributor guidance and post-deploy monitoring; an existing deterministic billing-invariant test can detect the malformed rule before deployment, but the deployment job does not currently require that result.
A proposed alternative for the comparison repository would require two human approvals for every repository change, including documentation-only changes.

review_context: A PR changes only the diagnostic evidence infrastructure used to qualify how a Gravity Flow Inbox settings flyout is observed; no production GPP rendering or workflow behavior is changed by the PR.

The PR acceptance boundary requires evidence that the host-owned Push Notification setting remains the authoritative native control and that the diagnostic cannot pass merely because unrelated notification-like content appears in the same flyout.
The evidence helper currently marks the setting as found when one visible textual match for the expected notification label is present in the settings flyout.
The helper does not currently require the matched text to be associated with the host-owned input element or another proven native-control provenance signal.
observed_evidence: The current authentic browser artifact contains one visible expected notification label and the reviewed run records that observation successfully.

The pinned Gravity Flow 3.1.0 runtime/source currently contains the flyout identity `.gform-flyout--inbox-settings` and the input identity `input[data-js="inbox-setting"][name="inbox-setting--push-enabled"]` for the native Push Notification setting.
The supplied evidence establishes those exact identities for the pinned runtime but does not establish that they are public or stable extension contracts across independently evolving host versions.

A future or variant flyout can contain an unrelated notification-like notice, browser-permission message, helper row, or decoy control whose visible wording can overlap the expected notification wording.

Direct inspection can determine whether the helper's current predicate is based only on unique visible text and a controlled decoy case can test whether unrelated notification-like content can satisfy that predicate.
No supplied evidence shows a second production defect, a host-ownership defect, or a need to change Gravity Flow behavior itself.
delivery_context: The final audience includes a non-technical Persian-speaking Owner who needs the decision and next action without dense hashes or CI mechanics in the primary explanation.

Standard bounded technical repair and verification are delegated to engineering when the causal boundary and method are sufficiently qualified; no product/business meaning needs an Owner choice in the supplied facts.

Any delegated implementation must use the exact fresh PR target, preserve host ownership, include evidence capable of distinguishing the intended repair from a superficially passing predicate, and report material planned-versus-actual deviation.
The review is expected to identify the exact next action needed to progress the PR rather than merely describe possible work.

review_context: This is the final meaningful technical review before a repair/defect-class closure decision becomes operational; no later independent engineering gate is expected.

The reviewed PR hardens a bounded CSS validator used to enforce a positive property contract on rules that target the Gravity Flow Inbox native root identified by the class tokens `gflow-inbox`, `gflow-grid`, and `gflow-common`.

A prior review demonstrated one bypass: when the native-root context appears on an outer CSS block and a nested child rule uses `&`, flat rule extraction can lose the outer semantic context before selector classification.
The proposed repair carries qualifying parent selector context into nested rules before classification and claims root-complete, fail-closed defect-class closure for native-root targeting.
The current inspected production stylesheet uses the canonical dot-class form for the native root and contains no observed production violation of the positive property contract.
control_evidence: The classifier directly recognizes the native-root identity when all three class tokens are present in the selector's admitted dot-class representation.

CSS also permits class-token membership to be expressed through an attribute token-match representation, and selectors can combine dot-class and attribute-token forms while preserving the same class-membership meaning.

The supplied classifier contract does not yet establish whether those equivalent or mixed representations are recognized as native-root targets or deterministically rejected before a positive classification can be missed.

The validator's final positive-evidence fallback includes a global `native_target_members > 0` condition rather than requiring every semantically native-targeting rule in a stylesheet to be positively classified.

A stylesheet can contain more than one rule, so a recognized canonical native-root rule and another rule with a semantically equivalent but differently represented native-root identity can coexist in the same realistic validation context.
No supplied evidence claims universal CSS parser coverage or support for every theoretically legal selector representation.
closure_context: The currently proposed code change is limited to preserving native-root context through nested-rule extraction; no authority/source-of-truth, public API/schema, persisted-state, runtime/topology, or external-consumer migration is described.
The requested final decision asks whether the repair can be accepted as safe to proceed and whether the same-root defect class and fail-closed mechanical enforcement can be considered closed.

For the exact reviewed Head, PR Inspector's controlled projection is `YELLOW / repair_and_verify`; Engineering Compass is being used to deepen causal/closure analysis and produce the engineering handoff, not to redefine PR Inspector projection semantics.

If engineering action is required, the next Executor receives a copy-ready prompt; the Owner-facing result should remain concise and practical in Persian and distinguish current production validity from any remaining protection/control issue.
